sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r9/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 3 (#2 instruction_preserves_natural_human_voice) and Internal Quality Checks row 3 (same text, no extra annotation)
evidence: Workbook #2 asks for an authentic human voice, not robotic/over-polished/LLM prose; skill quality-checks.md:14-15 says to look for sentence variety, contractions and terse fragments, and treats uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets or a voice that changes between brief and notes as defects. instruction.md reads as a firm member writing: it opens with a concrete grievance ('our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last', line 1), uses a short framing sentence ('Two things matter more than anything else.', line 3), contractions ('doesn't', 'we'll') and a plain request ('please try it the way we'll use it', line 9). The three notes keep the same first-person 'we/our/us' firm voice and give reasons for the rules ('People fix typos and figures', conversations.md:9; 'Our internet in court is patchy', conversations.md:31; 'a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us', walls-and-retention.md:61; 'That means everything sent today has the same time, which is why we care...', integration.md:42). There are 14 contractions across the files (including mustn't, won't, I'm, aren't). A grep for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|user-friendly|streamline|elevate|shall|em dash finds no hits. Apart from the necessary account table (walls-and-retention.md:49-55), the notes use prose paragraphs, not parallel bullet lists. The occasional switch to 'I' in conversations.md:25,33 ('When I open a matter', 'what I'm doing') is how a staff member would naturally write. It is not a change of register. Observation (not a defect): the notes are dense and enumerative in places, such as the list of routes a wall must cover (walls-and-retention.md:61) and the startup environment list (integration.md:38). That precision is tied to graded behaviour, and it stays in the firm's voice with stated reasons rather than shall/must spec tables. Counterexample attempt: a more casual, terser brief that leaves out these enumerations would read just as human but would lose fairness for later rows, so the current density is justified. No LLM-signature phrasing was found. This row is a text-only judgement and needs no runtime evidence, so the missing full grading run does not affect it.
